correctness.rationale: The selected rook vertices are edges of K_{p,q}; their induced line graph is a forest exactly when the selected edges form a linear forest. Opposite-shore unsaturated vertices in different components could be joined; if an A vertex is unsaturated, a B vertex must also be unsaturated because 2q exceeds the forest bound, and all components have an unsaturated vertex. This forces a spanning path and hence p=q. Otherwise A is saturated and has 2p selected incidences, which gives maximality in the unbalanced case. Counting alternating labeled paths gives the stated exponential series: equal positive shore sizes give one orientation choice from the A end, and unequal sizes require division by two. For maximal unbalanced forests c paths use p+c B vertices and the ordered positive compositions of p supply the binomial coefficient, with c! for unordered paths. Complements give the feedback-vertex-set claim. Independent rook-adjacency enumeration of all 64 subsets of the 2-by-3 board and all 32,768 of the 3-by-5 board confirms the counts and maximality, including the latter's 360 one-component and 180 two-component maxima.
